title: Elon Musk says Tesla plans to make an autonomous Model Y with no steering wheel
html:
Harald Tittel/picture alliance via Getty Images

Tesla Robotaxi uses a fleet of Model Ys, but the terms of service limit seating to 4 people.

Elon Musk said Tesla plans to develop a steering-wheel-free, pedal-free version of the Model Y capable of carrying six or seven passengers, though he didn't explain how the company would configure the vehicle's interior.

The Tesla CEO said on Wednesday at The New York Times DealBook Summit that the Cybercab — a two-seater coupe with no steering wheel or pedals — will cover most of the passenger miles driven for the company's robotaxi service, but the need for a bigger autonomous car is still there.

"If you've got a whole family in the car, you still need autonomous vehicles for that, so what we plan to do is have an autonomous version of Model Y that wouldn't have steering wheels and pedals and would be good for transporting groups of six or seven people," Musk said.

Tesla Robotaxi already uses Model Ys in its autonomous vehicle fleet, but it can transport only up to four passengers.

A robotaxi capable of carrying six or seven passengers would give Tesla a way to serve larger groups, a segment of the US autonomous ride-hailing market that remains relatively underserved.

Waymo's Ojai, which is supposed to be the company's more spacious vehicle platform compared to the Jaguar SUVs, can fit up to four people.

Uber plans to launch robotaxis with Lucid's Gravity SUV, which the ride-hailing company said can seat six people.
summary: Elon Musk said Tesla has plans to build an autonomous Model Y without a steering wheel to fit more passengers for the company's robotaxi service.
